pages.name: Meat room to vegetable room
pages.task: Drag the meat room to −20 °C. How far is it from the vegetable room?
pages.why: From −20 °C up to zero is 20 degrees, and from zero up to +4 °C is 4 more. So the two rooms are 20 + 4 = 24 degrees apart.

pages.alt: An upright number line from minus 24 degrees to plus 8 degrees, drawn like a thermometer, with zero marked, and readings at plus 4 degrees and minus 20 degrees. A hop down from plus 4 degrees to 0 degrees, 4 degrees. A hop down from 0 degrees to minus 20 degrees, 20 degrees. A bracket marks the gap, 24 degrees, 4 + 20 equals 24.

pages.why: Size is the gap from zero, so −12 V has size 12 V. The minus only says which side of zero it sits. Maths writes |−12| = 12 and calls size the modulus, or absolute value.

pages.why: Further from zero means a bigger size. −7 °C has size 7 and +5 °C has size 5, so −7 °C is further from zero, even though +5 °C is higher.

pages.task: The air is at −1.5 °C and the sea at +2.3 °C. How many degrees apart are they?
pages.why: From −1.5 °C up to zero is 1.5 degrees, and from zero up to +2.3 °C is 2.3 more. So they are 1.5 + 2.3 = 3.8 degrees apart.

pages.task: Which gap is bigger, A or B?
pages.why: A, from −8 °C to −3 °C, stays below zero, so it is 8 − 3 = 5 degrees. B, from −3 °C to +3 °C, crosses zero, so it is 3 + 3 = 6 degrees, the bigger gap.
